'''Adam Jonathan Burgasser''' is an American [[astrophysicist]] and professor of astronomy and astrophysics at the [[University of California, San Diego]] (UC San Diego).<ref name="ucsdfaculty" /><ref name="aas247" /> His research concerns the lowest-mass stars, [[brown dwarf]]s, and [[exoplanet]] host stars. His doctoral work contributed to the definition of the [[T dwarf|T spectral class]] of brown dwarfs,<ref name="caltechthesis" /><ref name="spectra2002" /> and he was a member of the teams that discovered the seven Earth-sized planets orbiting the ultracool dwarf star [[TRAPPIST-1]].<ref name="nature2017" /><ref name="ucsdnews2017" /> He served as vice president of the [[American Astronomical Society]] (AAS) from 2021 to 2024 and was named a Fellow of the AAS in 2026.<ref name="aasofficers" /><ref name="aasfellows" /> As an undergraduate he was an [[NCAA Division III]] national champion springboard diver.<ref name="ucsdhof" />

== Early life and education ==

Burgasser was raised in [[Buffalo, New York]], and graduated from Sweet Home High School.<ref name="ucsdhof" /> He received a BS in physics with highest distinction from UC San Diego in 1996,<ref name="congressbio" /> where he worked as an undergraduate researcher with astronaut [[Sally Ride]].<ref name="astrobites" /> As a UC San Diego undergraduate he competed in springboard diving, winning the 1996 NCAA Division III national championship in the 3-meter event and being named Division III Diver of the Year; he was a seven-time [[All-America|All-American]].<ref name="ucsdhof" />

He earned an MS (1999) and a PhD in physics with a minor in planetary science from the [[California Institute of Technology]],<ref name="congressbio" /><ref name="caltechthesis" /> where he was advised by [[Michael E. Brown]] and [[J. Davy Kirkpatrick]].<ref name="astrogen" /> His dissertation, ''The Discovery and Characterization of Methane-bearing Brown Dwarfs and the Definition of the T Spectral Class'', presented the discovery of methane-bearing brown dwarfs and helped establish the T spectral classification.<ref name="caltechthesis" />

== Career ==

Burgasser was a [[Hubble Fellowship|Hubble Postdoctoral Fellow]] at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] from 2001 to 2004 and a Spitzer Postdoctoral Fellow at the [[American Museum of Natural History]] from 2004 to 2005.<ref name="congressbio" /> He then joined the physics faculty of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] before moving to UC San Diego in 2010.<ref name="congressbio" /><ref name="coolstarlab" /> He is a professor in, and founding faculty member of, UC San Diego's Department of Astronomy and Astrophysics, established in 2023.<ref name="ucsdfaculty" /><ref name="coolstarlab" /> He was a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Scholar]] at the [[University of Exeter]] in 2017–2018.<ref name="congressbio" /><ref name="candidate2021" />

In April 2017, Burgasser testified before the [[United States House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology]] at a hearing on advances in the search for life beyond Earth.<ref name="hearing" />

Within the American Astronomical Society, Burgasser served as a councilor/trustee (2016–2019) and as vice president (2021–2024),<ref name="aasofficers" /> and chaired the AAS Committee on the Status of Minorities in Astronomy from 2013 to 2016.<ref name="candidate2021" /> He served on a science panel of the [[Decadal survey|Astro2020 decadal survey]].<ref name="candidate2021" />

== Research ==

Burgasser's research focuses on ultracool dwarfs — very-low-mass stars and brown dwarfs — including their discovery, spectral classification, atmospheres, multiplicity, and use as probes of Galactic structure.<ref name="conversation" /><ref name="aas247" /> Working with data from the [[2MASS|Two Micron All Sky Survey]], he co-authored early discoveries of L and T dwarfs,<ref name="2mass2000" /> and his papers on the near-infrared spectra of T dwarfs established a classification scheme for the class.<ref name="spectra2002" /><ref name="unified2006" /> He created the SpeX Prism Library, an archive of low-resolution near-infrared spectra of ultracool dwarfs, and the associated SPLAT analysis toolkit.<ref name="coolstarlab" /><!-- primary source only; consider trimming if reviewer objects -->

Burgasser was a co-author of the 2016 and 2017 ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' papers reporting the discovery of Earth-sized planets transiting TRAPPIST-1, contributing characterization of the ultracool host star,<ref name="nature2016" /><ref name="nature2017" /><ref name="ucsdnews2017" /> and led a 2017 study with Eric Mamajek estimating the age of the TRAPPIST-1 system at 5.4–9.8 billion years.<ref name="universetoday" />

In 2024, he led a study of CWISE J124909.08+362116.0, a low-mass star or brown dwarf identified by [[Backyard Worlds: Planet 9]] citizen scientists that is moving fast enough to escape the Milky Way's gravity.<ref name="nasa2024" /><ref name="keck" /> In 2025 he led the team reporting the first clear detection of [[phosphine]] in a brown dwarf atmosphere, in the object Wolf 1130C, published in ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''.<ref name="smithsonian" />

== Equity, education, and outreach ==

Burgasser co-organized the first Inclusive Astronomy conference at [[Vanderbilt University]] in 2015, directs the UC-HBCU physics bridge program linking UC San Diego with [[Morehouse College]] and [[Spelman College]], and has served on the steering committee of the [[Cal-Bridge]] program.<ref name="congressbio" /><ref name="candidate2021" /> He received UC San Diego's Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action and Diversity Award in 2014,<ref name="congressbio" /> the UC San Diego Academic Senate Distinguished Teaching Award in 2016,<ref name="teaching2016" /> and the School of Physical Sciences Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Excellence Award in 2023.<ref name="ucsdastronews" />

With education researcher Genevive Bjorn, Burgasser co-authored ''How to Critically Read the Scientific Research Literature: Introducing the CERIC Method'' ([[Cambridge University Press]], 2026), a guide to critical reading of primary scientific literature.<ref name="cupbook" /> He delivered a plenary lecture at the 247th AAS meeting in January 2026 on brown dwarfs as tracers of Galactic archaeology.<ref name="aas247" />

== Diving ==

Burgasser won the NCAA Division III national championship in 3-meter springboard diving in 1996 and was named the Division III Diver of the Year.<ref name="ucsdhof" /> He received the NCAA Silver Anniversary Award in 2021, the first UC San Diego recipient, and was inducted into the UC San Diego Athletics Hall of Fame in 2023.<ref name="ucsdhof" />
